claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for?** If yes, how many children are you inquiring about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 16 and lives at home with me. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I can see you have one child, Alex, who is 16 and lives at home with you.

Since Alex is 16, there are specific rules that apply. Let me ask you:

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he studying at school, college, or undertaking approved training?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. He's studying for his A-levels at the local sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Since Alex is 16 and in approved education (studying A-levels), that's a good start.

Now I need to ask you about your own circumstances:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. Now I need to understand a bit more about your situation:

**Do you have the right to reside in the UK?** For example, are you:
- A British citizen
- Someone with settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
- Someone who has moved to the UK with the right to reside

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm a British citizen. I've lived here all my life.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Are you the person responsible for Alex?** That is, does he live with you, and are you the one providing for his care (such as food, clothes, accommodation, etc.)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. He lives with me and I provide for all his needs - food, clothes, accommodation, everything he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One more important question:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (For example, Alex's other parent or another family member?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him. It's just me looking after him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me just check one final thing:

**Has Alex started any paid work for 24 hours or more per week, or is he claiming any benefits in his own right** (such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't. He's just focused on his A-levels at the moment - no job and he's not claiming any benefits himself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Based on the information you've provided, you meet all the requirements:

✅ **Alex qualifies** - Even though he's 16, Child Benefit can continue for children under 20 who stay in approved education or training. His A-level studies at sixth form college count as approved education.

✅ **You're responsible for Alex** - He lives with you and you provide for all his needs (food, clothes, accommodation).

✅ **You live in the UK** - You're a British citizen living in Manchester, which meets the residency requirements.

✅ **No one else is claiming** - Nobody else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

✅ **Alex isn't working full-time or claiming benefits** - He's focused on his studies and hasn't started work for 24+ hours per week, and he's not claiming benefits in his own right.

You can proceed with claiming Child Benefit for Alex. Just remember that if his circumstances change (for example, if he leaves education, starts working 24+ hours a week, or starts claiming certain benefits), you'll need to inform HMRC.

Also, be aware that if you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge.
